mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q01.stem: The 1.5 mm² marking of a stranded conductor indicates its cross-sectional area, not a diameter of 1.5 mm.
reasons: mm² is area and mm is length; check the correspondence in the application table.
This statement is true. mm² is area and mm is length; check the correspondence in the application table.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q02.stem: If the smallest graduation is 0.01 mm, the error is always within 0.01 mm under all conditions of use.
reasons: This statement is false. Orientation, contact and condition affect actual measurements.
Orientation, contact and condition affect actual measurements.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q03.stem: Even with a large measurement range, an instrument cannot be used on equipment exceeding its safety rating.
reasons: Functional range and safety rating are separate requirements.
This statement is true. Functional range and safety rating are separate requirements.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q04.stem: Product numbers and inspection-standard revisions have no bearing on traceability.
reasons: This statement is false. It is necessary to know what was assessed and against which standard.
It is necessary to know what was assessed and against which standard.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q05.stem: If the average is at the specification midpoint, every product is necessarily within specification.
reasons: This statement is false. The average and variation provide different information.
The average and variation provide different information.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q06.stem: Check line types to avoid mistaking a centerline for an outline to cut.
reasons: Different line types have different meanings.
This statement is true. Different line types have different meanings.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q07.stem: On a common four-band resistor, the third band is read as the multiplier.
reasons: Distinguish the first two bands, multiplier and tolerance.
This statement is true. Distinguish the first two bands, multiplier and tolerance.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q08.stem: Passing current through one diode always immediately produces perfectly smooth, constant DC.
reasons: This statement is false. Rectification and smoothing are different.
Rectification and smoothing are different.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q09.stem: Scheduled replacement can reduce failures while also incurring the cost of replacing parts that are still usable.
reasons: Consider both preventive benefits and replacement costs.
This statement is true. Consider both preventive benefits and replacement costs.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q10.stem: A voltage regulator’s supply stabilization differs from A/D conversion of a signal.
reasons: Power-supply functions and signal conversion are separate.
This statement is true. Power-supply functions and signal conversion are separate.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q11.stem: Measured grease penetration and all classification numbers always increase or decrease in the same direction.
reasons: This statement is false. Do not confuse different indication systems.
Do not confuse different indication systems.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q12.stem: Every device that opens contacts can safely interrupt short-circuit current without checking its ratings.
reasons: This statement is false. Check breaking capacity and application.
Check breaking capacity and application.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q13.stem: Logistics quality includes the correct goods, quantity, destination and promised delivery date.
reasons: Delivery accuracy is also a customer requirement.
This statement is true. Delivery accuracy is also a customer requirement.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q14.stem: Burrs on a cut surface affect appearance only and have no effect on installation.
reasons: This statement is false. Also inspect effects on subsequent processes.
Also inspect effects on subsequent processes.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q15.stem: The basic method for a common metalworking file is to apply maximum force only on the return stroke.
reasons: This statement is false. Release force on the return stroke.
Release force on the return stroke.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q16.stem: Combine company management with workers following procedures to reduce hazards.
reasons: These responsibilities do not replace one another.
This statement is true. These responsibilities do not replace one another.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q17.stem: Fire-extinguisher and AED signs help locate that equipment.
reasons: Distinguish equipment signs from evacuation signs.
This statement is true. Distinguish equipment signs from evacuation signs.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q18.stem: The three actuals principle always requires touching live parts with bare hands to establish the cause.
reasons: This statement is false. Direct verification also requires safe conditions.
Direct verification also requires safe conditions.
It is a management-system standard.
This statement is true. It is a management-system standard.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q20.stem: Every used or recovered battery has no voltage and may be short-circuited.
reasons: This statement is false. Remaining energy does not automatically disappear when a battery becomes used.
Remaining energy does not automatically disappear when a battery becomes used.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q21.stem: Diameter φ and radius R indicate different dimensions of a circle.
reasons: The diameter is twice the radius.
This statement is true. The diameter is twice the radius.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q22.stem: If a terminal hole fits the screw, no conductor-side compatibility check is needed.
reasons: This statement is false. Both sides must meet their applicable ranges.
Both sides must meet their applicable ranges.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q23.stem: Choose drills and end mills after checking cutting-edge locations and applications.
reasons: Match the applications of the machine and tool.
This statement is true. Match the applications of the machine and tool.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q24.stem: The only distinction between n-type and p-type is that the entire materials carry negative and positive charge respectively.
reasons: This statement is false. Understand carriers and impurities separately.
Understand carriers and impurities separately.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q25.stem: If the total quantity agrees, held products may be recorded as completed products.
reasons: This statement is false. Product states must also be identified.
Product states must also be identified.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q26.stem: Basic on-delay and off-delay timers delay different transitions.
reasons: Trace the timing of the on or off transition.
This statement is true. Trace the timing of the on or off transition.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q27.stem: One more failure always means a higher failure rate, regardless of operating hours.
reasons: This statement is false. A rate needs its denominator.
A rate needs its denominator.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q28.stem: In the negative-resist concept example, the protective film hardened by exposure remains.
reasons: Check which film remains for the process used.
This statement is true. Check which film remains for the process used.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q29.stem: Increasing the number of poles decreases synchronous speed at the same frequency.
reasons: Ns is inversely proportional to the number of poles.
This statement is true. Ns is inversely proportional to the number of poles.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q30.stem: Even if a ruler’s end is worn away, its reference point never changes on any design.
reasons: This statement is false. Check the reference-point design and condition.
Check the reference-point design and condition.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q01.stem: A resistor is marked 1 kΩ with a tolerance of ±5%. Which is its marked tolerance range?
reasons: 5% of 1000 Ω is 50 Ω, giving 950–1050 Ω. Also check ratings and inspection conditions.
This uses ±0.5%, one decimal order different from ±5%.
It omits the lower side and excludes the permitted 950–999 Ω range.
This is ±50%, rather than the specified ±5%.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q02.stem: Calculate the synchronous speed of a 50 Hz, six-pole induction machine using Ns=120 f/p.
reasons: 120×50/6=1000 min⁻¹. This is rotating-field speed, not a guarantee of actual rotor speed under load.
3000 is the synchronous speed for two poles at 50 Hz, not six poles.
Divide by six poles; do not multiply to get 36000.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q03.stem: A transformer’s secondary is unloaded while its primary receives voltage under rated conditions. Which judgment is appropriate?
options: With no load, the primary must also have no voltage.
Core loss may still occur; do not assume zero power or no hazard.
Touch the copper winding to check safety.
reasons: Supply voltage remains on the primary even when the secondary is unloaded.
Core loss due to changing flux can remain at no load. Primary voltage and hazards do not disappear.
Touching an energized winding risks electric shock and other harm.
Core flux and other conditions depend on frequency, so specified conditions cannot be ignored.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q04.stem: A component looks normal but may have been handled without ESD protection. What should you do?
options: Touch its terminals with bare hands to test performance.
Accept it unconditionally because no spark was seen.
Remove all packaging and leave it exposed.
Do not rule out damage from appearance alone; verify and identify it under the procedure.
reasons: Bare-hand contact may introduce further static electricity.
ESD damage may occur without a visible spark.
Leaving it unpackaged removes protection against ESD and other hazards.
ESD damage may be invisible. Follow the handling-history, inspection and hold procedures.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q05.stem: The number of failures is unchanged from last year, but operating hours halved. What is needed for comparison?
options: Shorten the replacement interval as far as possible without evidence.
Assume the same condition because failure counts match.
Discard records and do not compare.
Account for operating hours, production volume and other conditions.
reasons: An unsupported interval reduction does not evaluate the comparison or establish appropriate replacement.
With half the hours, the same count changes the failures-per-hour comparison.
Discarding records prevents comparison including operating conditions.
Failure counts alone cannot establish condition. Also review use conditions, downtime and repair details.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q06.stem: A wire has shifted at a terminal whose solder has not solidified. What is appropriate?
options: Pull it hard just before solidification.
Skip cooling and bend the neighboring terminal.
Keep the joint still during cooling, then check rework under the criteria.
Ship without inspection if the joint is shiny.
reasons: Pulling during solidification moves the joint and can cause a bad connection.
Bending the neighboring part before cooling transmits force to and disturbs the joint.
Movement during solidification disrupts the joint. Inspect after cooling, then use approved rework and reassessment.
Shininess alone cannot establish the joint’s condition or internal defects.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q07.stem: A relay’s coil voltage matches, but its contact capacity is below the load. What is appropriate?
options: Use it unconditionally because the coil matches.
Assume an SSR needs no heat check.
Find suitable equipment that also meets contact requirements.
Remove load protection and use it.
reasons: The contact capacity is insufficient; coil voltage alone is not enough.
SSRs also require rating checks for heating, heat dissipation and other conditions.
Coil and contacts have separate ratings. Shape and coil voltage alone do not establish load-switching suitability.
Removing protection does not resolve insufficient capacity and increases fault hazards.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q08.stem: Someone proposes adding gloves for work near a rotating drill press. How should this be assessed?
options: Grab rotating chips with cotton work gloves.
Check entanglement hazards and required PPE in the work procedure.
Assume gloves always improve safety for every job.
reasons: The gloves and hand may be pulled in by rotating chips.
Gloves can create entanglement hazards depending on the task. Match training and PPE to the specific hazards.
Gloves can be caught by rotating parts and are not universally safer.
OJT does not remove the need to check safety procedures and PPE.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q09.stem: Dimensions changed after a material lot change despite the same tool settings. What should be checked?
options: Compare 4 M changes, including material, and measurement conditions.
Decide the operator is the only cause.
Rewrite only the average to the specification midpoint.
reasons: 4 M includes people, machines, materials and methods. Investigate changes and results using actual items and records.
The material lot changed, so the cause cannot be restricted to the operator.
Rewriting data changes neither dimensions nor cause and destroys record reliability.
Discarding lot records prevents relating the change timing to dimensional changes.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q10.stem: Five boxes contain 12 products each, but the delivery note states 54. What discrepancy needs verification?
options: Reducing cushioning will reconcile the quantity.
The actual total is 60, six more than the note’s 54.
Ignore the quantity difference if the destination matches.
reasons: Cushioning quantity does not resolve a product-count discrepancy.
12×5=60. Find the cause of the six-unit difference and reconcile goods and documents before dispatch.
A correct destination does not resolve an incorrect quantity.
12×5=60 actual products, not 54.
